evidence.summary: Account age has a strong positive relationship with score (Spearman rho = +0.816). Controlled experiments also showed score increasing as account_age_days increased while other parameters were held fixed.
Months active has a strong negative relationship with score (Spearman rho = -0.807). Controlled experiments also showed score decreasing as months_active increased under fixed configurations.

Trust score has a strong negative marginal relationship with score (Spearman rho = -0.732). Controlled experiments indicate the relationship is non-monotonic, with a higher-scoring region around approximately 345-355 and substantially lower scores at high trust_score values.
Utilisation has a strong positive relationship with score (Spearman rho = +0.657). Controlled observations also showed lower scores when utilisation was reduced from 1.0 to 0.95 and 0.90.

Channel shows a small observed score difference across categories. Controlled observations showed channel D producing the highest score among A-D, but the magnitude was much smaller than the effects observed for the stronger features.
